item.title: Now the hard part
item.description: When a country loses a war, the winner dictates the peace terms. This is abundantly clear in the memorandum of understanding. The US and Israel still can’t comprehend that Iran won their war of choice. Also, despite the media hype of ‘Ukraine is winning’ , the reality is that time is running out for Kiev and its western backers. CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Tarik Cyril Amar.

item.title: Defeat and humiliation
item.description: At least on paper Iran has won a historic victory over the United States. The MoU demands the US recognize Iran as a legitimate and even powerful state actor. Iran defeated two nuclear states – the US and Israel. Can it now win the peace? CrossTalking with Mohammad Marandi, Ali H. Mourad, and Zaid Belbagi.

item.title: Deal theater?
item.description: We have been repeatedly told there is a deal to be had ending the unprovoked war on Iran. A deal means there is rough consensus. Given the parties involved that consensus seems a near impossibility. Also, are Kaja Kallas’s days numbered as the EU top diplomat? We can only hope. CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Mark Sleboda.

item.title: Massive escalation
item.description: In order to be a great power today, a country must have deterrence. This is what the EU and NATO want to deny Russia. This explains why their proxy Ukraine has become heavily reliant on drone warfare while it is losing on the battlefield. This in turn brings about escalation. And this is becoming dangerous for all involved. CrossTalking with Dan Kovalik, Michael Maloof, and Ryan Milton.

item.title: Pause, not peace
item.description: What are we to make of the memorandum of understanding ending the US-Israel war on Iran? At this point it would seem to be more of a pause than a peace process. Nothing has been resolved. And the headwinds against a final agreement are enormous. The trust deficit remains. CrossTalking with Muhannad Ayyash, Helena Cobban, and Foad Izadi.

item.title: Peace without peace
item.description: Wars are easy to start but very difficult to end. Donald Trump is learning this the hard way. The American president is clearly looking for an exit from this conflict. His partner in this war is Israel. Israel has very different ideas. CrossTalking with Raed Jarrar, Elijah J. Magnier, and Hamidreza Gholamzadeh.

item.title: Return to war
item.description: If you have been following the unprovoked war on Iran, you have been provided with at least two opposite interpretations. According to one, the war is Iran’s fault and it has been defeated. The other holds that the US and Israel have suffered a strategic defeat. One thing is for sure – this conflict is far from over. CrossTalking with Jenin Younes, Ali Mamouri and Daoud Kuttab.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Insults as strategy
item.description: Theatrics is not a substitute for strategy. Zelensky’s insulting letter to the Russian president is a reflection of the West’s inability to negotiate in good faith. Also, Germany’s denial of a seat on the UN Security Council demonstrates Berlin’s fading importance in the world. This can also be said of Europe in general. CrossTalking with Mark Sleboda and George Szamuely.
